questions.question: If x+2y = 14 and x-y = 5 then find x. यदि x+2y = 14 और x-y = 5 है तो x ज्ञात कीजिए।
questions.solution:
Here, x + 2y = 14 and x − y = 5.

Subtract second from first: (x+2y) − (x−y) = 14 − 5 → 3y = 9 → y = 3.

Then x = 5 + y = 8.

GM Karthik Venkataraman won the 61st National Chess Championship (2024 - 25) in Gurgaon and received ₹6 lakh.

Key Insights -

•Organized by All India Chess Federation.

• Format: Swiss system.

• IM Neelash Saha was among top ranks but not tiebreak finalist.

• Event saw strong representation of Indian GMs.

• Encourages emerging talent for international events.

• Chess in India rising post-Viswanathan Anand era.

• India hosted FIDE Chess Olympiad 2022.

• Gurgaon event part of national ranking circuit.

•Bharatanatyam is the oldest, mentioned in ancient Sangam texts (as "Sadir").

•Kathak developed during the Bhakti movement and Mughal era.

•Manipuri gained recognition later during medieval times in northeastern India.

•Mohiniyattam, with earliest records in Kerala temples, emerged most recently among these.

Key Insights -

•Bharatanatyam originated in Tamil Nadu; tied to Natya Shastra.

• Kathak evolved in northern India's courts and temples.

• Manipuri highlights Vaishnav devotional themes.

• Mohiniyattam derived from the legend of "Mohini," the female avatar of Vishnu.

•Classical dances preserve temple traditions and local storytelling.

• Indian classical dance uses "Nritta, Nritya, Natya" as its structural basis.

•Natya Shastra is the foundational text for all classical dance forms.

•Each form links to a specific geographic and linguistic culture.

"Mangrove Cell" of Maharashtra protects coastal biodiversity and promotes mangrove conservation and ecotourism.

Key Insights -

•Established in 2012 under State Forest Department.

• First dedicated unit for mangrove protection in India.

• Manages wetlands across Mumbai, Raigad, Thane.

• Introduced Mangrove Safari at Thane Creek.

• Works with local fisher communities.

•Maharashtra has India's largest urban mangrove cover.

• Collaborates with Mangrove Foundation for education.

• Supports MISHTI initiative under national policy.

BNSS (2023) allows confessions and statements during investigation to be video-recorded, improving transparency and accountability in criminal procedure.

Key Insights -

•BNSS replaces the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) 1973.

• Focuses on technology integration in justice system.

• Provides for electronic summons and FIRs.

• Mandates forensic team visit for serious crimes.

• Allows trials via video conferencing.

• Retains key procedural safeguards for accused.

• Part of three new criminal laws alongside BNS and BSA.

• Strengthens evidence collection through digital methods.

Article 334 ended Anglo-Indian nomination; 104th Amendment (2020) removed reserved Anglo-Indian seats in Lok Sabha and State Assemblies.

Key Insights -

•Earlier, one member could be nominated by the President (Lok Sabha) and Governor (State Assembly).

•Introduced under Articles 331 and 333.

• Intended to ensure community representation post-independence.

• Abolition reflected demographic and integration changes.

• 104th Amendment extended SC/ST reservation till 2030.

• Passed under NDA government.

• Anglo-Indian community historically small and urban.

• Marks transition toward uniform democratic representation.

Harvinder Singh won India's first Paralympic gold in archery at the 2024 Paris Games.

Key Insights -

•Event: Men's Recurve category.

• Represents Punjab.

• Also won bronze at Tokyo 2020.

• Uses specially modified bow.

• India's overall medal tally at Paris 2024 highest so far.

• Showcased India's rise in para-sports.

• First Indian archer (Olympic or Paralympic) to win gold.

• Encouraged by Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS).

Non-metallic minerals like limestone, mica, gypsum, and phosphorite are key to India's industrial base.

Key Insights -

•Used in cement, fertilizer, ceramics, glass industries.

• Found in Rajasthan, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh.

• India is a major mica exporter.

• Limestone crucial for steel and cement production.

• Gypsum used for plaster and fertilizer.

• Minerals are categorized as metallic, non-metallic, and energy.

• Non-metallics don't yield metals when melted.

• Essential for construction and infrastructure growth.

Kalbelia dance of Rajasthan imitates the graceful movements of serpents performed by the Kalbelia community.

Key Insights -

•Recognized as UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage (2010).

• Performed traditionally by snake charmers' community.

• Female dancers wear black swirling skirts symbolizing snakes.

• Accompanied by "been" and "dholak."

• Songs describe mythology and desert life.

• Originates from Pushkar, Jaisalmer, Jodhpur regions.

• Costumes decorated with mirror and embroidery work.

• Represents resilience of nomadic traditions.

Iron and steel is heavy industry due to heavy raw materials like iron ore, coal, and limestone - not lightweight materials.

Key Insights -

•Heavy industries produce capital goods (machines, metals).

• Iron and steel serve as foundation of industrial economy.

•Major Indian centers: Jamshedpur, Bhilai, Rourkela.

•Require high capital and energy input.

• Classified under basic industries.

• Use both blast furnace and electric arc methods.

• Backbone for engineering, construction, and defense.

• Contributes significantly to GDP and exports.

Soil pH is not a weather element; it belongs to pedology, not meteorology.

Key Insights -

•Weather elements: temperature, humidity, wind, precipitation, pressure.

• Soil pH affects agriculture, not weather.

• Climate is the long-term average of weather.

• Meteorological instruments include barometer, hygrometer, anemometer.

• IMD records and analyzes weather data.

• Weather determines short-term atmospheric conditions.

• Elements interact to shape local climate patterns.

• Soil properties belong to geophysical studies.

Cricket balls are standardized to ensure consistent play; any difference affects aerodynamics and fairness.

Key Insights -

•Standard ball: weight 155.9 - 163 g; circumference 22.4 - 22.9 cm.

• Red, white, and pink balls differ in coating but follow same size limits.

• Heavier balls swing less, lighter bounce more.

• Seam height influences swing.

• ICC ensures uniform conditions globally.

• Used leather casing with cork core.

•Maintenance affects performance (shine, roughness).

• Fair regulation maintains competitive balance.

Article 370 was abrogated through Presidential Order (C.O. 272) and resolution passed by Parliament on 5 August 2019, using Article 370(3).

Key Insights -

•Removed J&K's special constitutional status.

• Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019 bifurcated state into two UTs.

• Implemented by Home Ministry under PM Narendra Modi.

• Enabled uniform application of Indian laws.

• Abrogation followed Supreme Court validation process.

•Historic event altering federal framework.

•Promoted integration and central governance.

•Supported under Article 356 proclamation in the state at that time.

PSLV is called ISRO's "workhorse" because of its reliability and versatility in launching diverse payloads into various orbits, including Earth observation and navigation satellites.

Key Insights -

•First PSLV launch: 1993.

• Developed under ISRO's Satellite Launch Vehicle program.

• Can launch up to 1,750 kg to Sun-synchronous orbit.

• Notable missions: Chandrayaan-1, Mangalyaan, Cartosat.

• Over 95% success rate across variants.

• Capable of multi-satellite deployments.

•Variants include PSLV-XL, PSLV-CA, PSLV-DL.

• Contributed to India's reputation for low-cost, high-precision launches.

•Phamsana roofs are stepped or inclined slabs that rise to a single apex, typical of early Nagara temple styles.

Key Insights -

• Latina type has curvilinear (rekha-prasada) tower.

•Valabhi has a barrel-shaped roof.

•Phamsana temples are low and broad, unlike Latina spires.

• Nagara architecture is North Indian temple style.

• Found prominently in central and northern India.

•Phamsana often used for subsidiary shrines.

• Distinguishes from Dravidian (pyramidal) roof types.

• Key example: temples at Khajuraho.

MISHTI (Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats & Tangible Incomes) promotes mangrove plantation with scientific methods, announced in Union Budget 2023 - 24. It does not involve commercial leasing.

Key Insights -

•Aims at restoring mangrove ecosystems.

• Implemented jointly by MoEFCC and State Forest Departments.

• Enhances carbon sequestration and biodiversity.

• Linked to coastal livelihood programs.

• Uses CAMPA and MGNREGS funds.

• States covered: Gujarat, Odisha, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal, Maharashtra.

• Prevents coastal erosion and sea-level impacts.

• Complements Blue Economy vision.

"Hot Stage" compiles plays exploring Indian society, politics, and culture.

Key Insights -

•Written by contemporary Indian playwrights.

• Edited by academician theatre experts.

•Reflects urban realities and changing values.

• Focus on themes like identity, gender, and reform.

• Published as part of modern drama anthologies.

• English translations available.

• Highlights postcolonial Indian theatre.

• Promotes experimental stage writing.

•Pongtu is an agricultural festival of the Tutsa tribe, celebrated before millet harvest to honor deity Rangkhothak.

Key Insights -

•Pongtu means "community celebration."

• Celebrated with dance, songs, and indigenous rituals.

• Held mainly in Arunachal Pradesh's Changlang district.

• Associated with the agricultural calendar.

• Tutsa tribe follows animistic beliefs mixed with Rangfraism.

• Promotes unity and good harvest.

• Similar harvest festivals: Mopin (Galo), Solung (Adi), Reh (Idu Mishmi).

• Rangkhothak is seen as a protective and fertility deity.

Chotanagpur Plateau is indeed an eastern extension of Central Highlands. However, it is drained by Damodar, Subarnarekha, and Mahanadi - not Chambal or Betwa.

Key Insights -

•Lies in Jharkhand, parts of Odisha, Chhattisgarh, and Bihar.

• Composed mainly of Archean rocks.

• Rich in iron, coal, and mica.

• Major rivers: Damodar, Subarnarekha, Koel, Sankh.

• Known for Ranchi and Hazaribagh plateaus.

• Important industrial belt.

• Acts as source region for peninsular rivers.

• Plateau region supports tribal population concentration.

Switzerland ranked 1st in Infrastructure dimension in IMD World Competitiveness Rankings for both 2024 and 2025.

Key Insights -

•IMD Index evaluates economic performance, infrastructure, efficiency, and government performance.

•Switzerland known for transport, education, healthcare excellence.

• Maintains consistent high human capital indices.

• Infrastructure includes digital, physical, and energy systems.

• Singapore and Denmark follow Switzerland closely.

• India improved ranking due to business efficiency growth.

• IMD is based in Lausanne, Switzerland.

• Focuses on long-term national competitiveness.

First module of Bharatiya Antriksh Station (BAS) is planned for launch by 2028 under ISRO's human spaceflight program.

Key Insights -

•Part of India's long-term space station project.

• To follow Gaganyaan mission success.

• BAS aims for full functionality by 2035.

• Will conduct microgravity and life-science research.

• India's first independent space station.

• Collaboration with national research labs.

• Strengthens India's LEO operations capability.

• Supports docking of crew modules from HLVM3.

Under Article 352, a National Emergency proclamation must be approved by both Houses within one month.

Key Insights -

•Extension thereafter valid for 6 months at a time.

• Can be revoked anytime by President.

• Introduced first during Indo-China war 1962.

• Only national emergency can alter distribution of powers.

• State and financial emergencies have separate provisions.

• Article 353 outlines executive consequences.

• Article 358 suspends Article 19 rights.

• Parliamentary approval ensures checks and balances.

In Teen Taal (16 beats: 4+4+4+4), the Khali (empty beat) is marked on the 9th matra.

•Teen Taal is the most common Hindustani taal.

• Has four vibhags (sections).

•Clapping occurs on 1, 5, 13; wave on 9.

•Played in 16-beat cycles on tabla.

• Commonly used in khayal, thumri, and instrumental music.

• "Sam" is the first beat of the cycle.

• Taal gives rhythm framework in Indian classical music.

• Khali adds variation to rhythmic composition.

Launched by MoS Shri Shripad Naik on Electrical Safety Day 2025 to raise awareness on electrical hazard prevention.

Key Insights -

•Promotes public safety and best practices in electrical use.

•Supported by Ministry of Power.

• Focus on household and industrial safety norms.

• Encourages use of ISI-certified devices.

• Aims to reduce accidents from electric faults.

• Mascot symbolizes energy safety and vigilance.

• Linked with India's "Surakshit Bijli" campaign.

• Promotes adoption of e-learning safety modules.

India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) provides financial inclusion and basic banking through postal network and postmen (Gramin Dak Sevaks).

Key Insights -

•Launched in 2018 under Department of Posts.

• Offers savings, current accounts, remittances.

• 100% government-owned public sector bank.

• Uses doorstep banking via postmen.

• Aims for rural inclusion and financial literacy.

• Operates through over 1.5 lakh post offices.

• Offers AEPS, DBT, and digital payment services.

• Integrated with PM Jan Dhan Yojana ecosystem.

The BRICS Foreign Ministers' meeting of 2018 was held in Pretoria, hosted by South Africa.

Key Insights -

•BRICS: Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa.

• Focused on multilateralism and global south cooperation.

• Theme: "Collaboration for Inclusive Growth."

•10th BRICS Summit held same year in Johannesburg.

•Discussed UNSC reform and counterterrorism.

• South Africa joined BRICS in 2010.

• BRICS countries represent ~40% of global population.

• BRICS Bank is now called the New Development Bank.

questions.question: A sentence is provided in direct speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding indirect speech. He said, "I am not feeling well."
questions.questionHtml:
A sentence is provided in direct speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding indirect speech.

He said, "I am not feeling well."

options.text: He said that he is not feeling well.
options.html: He said that he is not feeling well.

options.text: He said that he was not feeling well.
options.html: He said that he was not feeling well.

options.text: He said that he didn't felt well.
options.html: He said that he didn't felt well.

options.text: He said he not feeling well.
options.html: He said he not feeling well.

questions.solution:
− Rule: In indirect speech, if the reporting verb ("said") is in the past tense, the tense of the reported speech moves one step back - present continuous → past continuous.

− So, "I am not feeling well" → "he was not feeling well."

− Other options:

− (1) fails to backshift tense.

− (3) uses "didn't felt" - double past form error.

− (4) missing "was" - grammatically incomplete.

questions.question: Change the following from active to passive: Why did the editor overlook the substantial stylistic anomalies?
questions.questionHtml:
Change the following from active to passive:

Why did the editor overlook the substantial stylistic anomalies?

options.text: Why have the substantial stylistic anomalies been overlooked by the editor?
options.html: Why have the substantial stylistic anomalies been overlooked by the editor?

options.text: Why are the substantial stylistic anomalies being overlooked by the editor?
options.html: Why are the substantial stylistic anomalies being overlooked by the editor?

options.text: Why did the substantial stylistic anomalies be overlooked by the editor?
options.html: Why did the substantial stylistic anomalies be overlooked by the editor?

options.text: Why were the substantial stylistic anomalies overlooked by the editor?
options.html: Why were the substantial stylistic anomalies overlooked by the editor?

questions.solution:
− Rule: In passive voice, the verb "did overlook" changes to "were overlooked."

− Structure: why + auxiliary (were) + subject + past participle (overlooked) + agent (by the editor).

− Other options:

− (1) uses present perfect, incorrect tense.

− (2) changes tense to continuous, altering meaning.

− (3) incorrect verb form "did be overlooked" - grammatically impossible.

questions.question: A sentence is provided in indirect speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding direct speech. The manager told the staff that deadlines must be followed strictly.
questions.questionHtml:
A sentence is provided in indirect speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding direct speech.

The manager told the staff that deadlines must be followed strictly.

options.text: "Deadlines must be followed strictly", said the manager.
options.html: "Deadlines must be followed strictly", said the manager.

options.text: "You should follow deadlines strictly", said the manager.
options.html: "You should follow deadlines strictly", said the manager.

options.text: "Deadlines are to be followed", said the manager.
options.html: "Deadlines are to be followed", said the manager.

questions.solution:
Rule: In reported speech, when the reporting verb is "told" and the original statement contains "must," we retain "must" in direct speech because it expresses obligation.

− Correct reconstruction: "Deadlines must be followed strictly," said the manager.

− Other options:

− (2) changes "must" to "should," altering meaning.

− (3) changes it into an imperative.

− (4) rephrases completely - different structure.

questions.question: Convert the sentence provided below from its passive voice structure to an active voice structure: It has been alleged that confidential data was being leaked by insiders within the firm.
questions.questionHtml:
Convert the sentence provided below from its passive voice structure to an active voice structure:

It has been alleged that confidential data was being leaked by insiders within the firm.

options.text: Insiders were leaking confidential data within the firm.
options.html: Insiders were leaking confidential data within the firm.

options.text: Confidential data had been leaked by insiders, it is alleged.
options.html: Confidential data had been leaked by insiders, it is alleged.

options.text: Insiders have allegedly been leaking confidential data within the firm.
options.html: Insiders have allegedly been leaking confidential data within the firm.

options.text: The firm was allegedly leaking insider data.
options.html: The firm was allegedly leaking insider data.

questions.solution:
− Rule: When converting passive to active, the subject and agent swap positions.

− "It has been alleged that + passive clause" → becomes "have allegedly been + verb-ing."

− Correct structure retains tense (present perfect continuous) and the reporting nature ("allegedly").

− Other options:

− (1) omits "allegedly" and changes tense.

− (2) shifts to past perfect.

− (4) changes the subject entirely.

questions.question: Rearrange the following sentences in correct order to make a logical passage: 1) The team analyzed the survey data. 2) Insights were used to improve the customer experience. 3) A targeted marketing campaign was created. 4) The data was collected through various channels.
questions.questionHtml:
Rearrange the following sentences in correct order to make a logical passage:

1) The team analyzed the survey data.

2) Insights were used to improve the customer experience.

3) A targeted marketing campaign was created.

4) The data was collected through various channels.
questions.solution:
Sentence 4 is the necessary starting point, as data must be collected before it can be analyzed or used. Sentence 1 logically follows the collection step (Sentence 4). Once collected, the data must be analyzed. Sentence 3 has a common, direct application of insights or findings derived from analyzing data (Sentence 1). It represents the immediate action taken. Sentence 2 represents the ultimate goal or outcome of the entire process, which is a broader result of using the insights gained from the analysis (Sentence 1) and subsequent action (Sentence 3).

Logical sequence = 4-1-3-2.

questions.question: Rearrange the following sentences to form a coherent paragraph: 1) These factors include the amount of sunlight received, the composition of the atmosphere, and the Earth's orbit. 2) The long-term variations in Earth's climate are influenced by a complex interplay of natural and anthropogenic factors. 3) The most significant anthropogenic factor is the emission of greenhouse gases from industrial activities. 4) Together, these elements determine the planet's overall energy balance and, consequently, its average temperature.
questions.questionHtml:
Rearrange the following sentences to form a coherent paragraph:

1) These factors include the amount of sunlight received, the composition of the atmosphere, and the Earth's orbit.

2) The long-term variations in Earth's climate are influenced by a complex interplay of natural and anthropogenic factors.

3) The most significant anthropogenic factor is the emission of greenhouse gases from industrial activities.

4) Together, these elements determine the planet's overall energy balance and, consequently, its average temperature.
questions.solution:
Sentence 2 introduces the main topic: long-term climate variations and the two types of influencing factors. Sentence 1 immediately follows and elaborates on the natural factors mentioned in sentence 2. Sentence 4 concludes the discussion of the combined natural elements/factors and their effect on the climate system's outcome. Sentence 3 shifts the focus to the anthropogenic factor introduced in sentence 2, providing the most important example.

The correct order for the sentences is 2-1-4-3.

questions.question: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error: The more senior the position was (1)/ the more urgent became the need (2)/ for discretion, decorum, and (3)/ refraining from premature disclosure. (4)
questions.questionHtml:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

The more senior the position was (1)/ the more urgent became the need (2)/ for discretion, decorum, and (3)/ refraining from premature disclosure. (4)
questions.solution:
− Rule: Parallelism - when items are listed in a series, grammatical forms must match.

− Error: "Refraining" breaks the parallel structure; the other nouns "discretion" and "decorum" are abstract nouns, not verbs or gerunds.

− Correction: "...for discretion, decorum, and refrain from premature disclosure" → all are now noun forms.

− Other parts are correct: "The more...the more..." is a correct comparative correlative.

questions.question: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error: The report's emphasis on techno-optimism, while commendable, (1) / overlook the structural inequities (2) / that persist in data accessibility and digital literacy (3) / across demographic and regional divides. (4)
questions.questionHtml:

The report's emphasis on techno-optimism, while commendable, (1) / overlook the structural inequities (2) / that persist in data accessibility and digital literacy (3) / across demographic and regional divides. (4)
questions.solution:

− Correct sentence: "The report's emphasis on techno-optimism, while commendable, overlooks the structural inequities.."

questions.question: Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence: She insisted me to take the medicine .
questions.questionHtml:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:

She insisted me to take the medicine.
questions.solution:
− Rule: After verbs like "insist," "suggest," "demand," or "recommend," we use that + subject + base verb (the subjunctive mood).

− Correct form: "She insisted that I take the medicine."

− Why others are wrong:

− "Insisted me to" is incorrect because "insist" is not followed by an object + infinitive.

− "Me that I take" repeats the subject wrongly.

− "To take medicine by me" is a passive infinitive - ungrammatical here.

− Correct structure: "No one knows where he is hiding."

− Wrong forms:

− (1) uses "is he" - inversion used only in direct questions.

− (2) ends with "at," which is redundant.

− (4) awkward structure with extra "is."

questions.question: Select the correct option: So, delicate ____________ the negotiations that a single leak could derail them.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the correct option:

So, delicate ____________ the negotiations that a single leak could derail them.
questions.solution:
− Rule: Subject - verb agreement. The subject here is the singular noun phrase "the negotiations" treated as one event - "So, delicate was the negotiation that..." is an example of inversion after 'so + adjective' for emphasis.

− Correct form: "So, delicate was the negotiation that..." (meaning: The negotiations are so delicate that...)

− Why others are wrong:

− "are" and "were" are in plural form.

"Is" is incorrect as "could" reflects the past tense in the sentence.

questions.question: Select the correct option: Her interpretation was_____________than insightful; it bordered on the revelatory.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the correct option:

Her interpretation was_____________than insightful; it bordered on the revelatory.
questions.solution:

− Meaning: Her interpretation was beyond insightful - it was almost revelatory.

− Other options:

− "less than" would mean below insightful.

− "other than" means different from, grammatically mismatched.

− "rather" adds emphasis, but "rather than" changes the sense to comparison.
